analysis:
This PR adds a `desktop_account` device-code purpose to the console `/link` flow. It is console UI plus docs only. The console and backend are out of scope for this provider threat model; the device-login tokens in A-008 are the closest asset.

Changed behavior:
- console-ui/src/app/link/page.tsx head:8 takes `purpose` from the attacker-controllable query string `?purpose=desktop_account`. It changes only the page copy and the prop passed to the form.
- DeviceLinkForm.tsx head:45 sends `{user_code, purpose}` to `/api/device/approve`. The docs (console-ui.md head patch @@-96) say the proxy forwards the body unchanged.
- The docs state the coordinator checks `purpose` against the code. Under that check, a crafted link cannot relabel a provider code as read-only desktop access.
- DeviceLinkForm.tsx head:62 checks `data.purpose` only after the server has already approved. It is a UI confirmation, not a control.
  - If a coordinator ignores `purpose` (for example an older one), the desktop flow may have approved a provider-scoped code. The user then sees an error, but the remote approval stands.
  - Whether a provider token was actually issued depends on backend behavior, which is platform-owned and not supplied.
- Head:217 tells users the grant is 30-day, cannot start providers, manage API keys or withdraw funds. This claim cannot be verified from the supplied source.
- Device-code phishing in general is pre-existing.

No provider WebSocket, attestation, encryption or key-handling code changed. A-008 (provider tokens) and TB-002 are unaffected unless the platform issues desktop tokens that are accepted for provider registration. Deeper review should confirm in darkbloom-platform:
- POST /v1/device/approve rejects a purpose mismatch.
- `desktop_account` tokens are read-only and rejected for provider WebSocket registration.
